text: {"question":"How do the generalized PAge parameterizations discussed in the first passage and the CPL dark‑energy model examined in the second passage together influence the resolution of the Hubble tension when both late‑time and CMB data are considered?","reference_answer":"The GPAge models, by extending the PAge framework to higher redshift and improving low‑z accuracy, can alleviate or even resolve the Hubble tension when CMB data are included, and they are strongly favored over ΛCDM. The CPL parametrization, which allows the dark‑energy equation of state to evolve and cross the phantom divide, also shows a preference for easing the tension, especially when DESI BAO and full‑shape data are combined with CMB and SN observations. Together, these two approaches suggest that both early‑time modifications (via GPAge) and late‑time evolving dark energy (via CPL) can jointly reduce the discrepancy in H0, with the combined data sets providing a more robust alleviation of the Hubble tension than either model alone."}
